    s = s.replace("import { nextCharge }", "import { monthlyCents, nextCharge }")
    s = s.replace("// how many months one charge pays for\nconst MONTHS = { monthly: 1, yearly: 12 };\n\n", "")
    return s.replace("Math.floor(sub.price / MONTHS[sub.cycle])", "monthlyCents(sub)")

def renewals(s):
    return s.replace("a.when.localeCompare(b.when)", "a.date.localeCompare(b.date)")

def cli(s):
    s = s.replace("import { CYCLE, monthlyCents }", "import { CYCLE, monthlyCents, monthlyTwelfths, roundTwelfths }")
    s = s.replace("[--every month|year]", "[--every week|month|year]")
    s = re.sub(r"// how much of one charge.*\nconst SHARE_PER_MONTH.*\n\n", "", s)
    s = s.replace("// --every month|year (monthly/yearly work too)\nconst EVERY = {",
                  "// --every week|month|year (weekly/monthly/yearly work too)\nconst EVERY = { week: CYCLE.WEEK, weekly: CYCLE.WEEK,")

    s = s.replace("cut to the cent once", "round to the cent once")

    return s.replace("Later charges fall on the same day of the month, or the last day of a shorter month.",

# subtrack

Keep track of your subscriptions from the terminal: what they cost you each month, and what renews next.
Plain Node.js (ES modules), no dependencies.

```sh
subtrack add Netflix 12.99                        # monthly by default, first charge today
subtrack add "Domain name" 14 --every year --since 2026-03-02
subtrack list                                     # every plan with its monthly cost
subtrack total                                    # what all of it costs you a month
subtrack renewals --within 14                     # charges coming up in the next 14 days, soonest first
subtrack export > subs.csv                        # CSV for a spreadsheet
subtrack remove Netflix
```

During development, run it with `node bin/subtrack.js <command>`.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--every month\|year` | add | How often the plan charges you (default `month`). |
| `--since YYYY-MM-DD` | add | Date of the first charge (default today). Later charges fall on the same day of the month, or the last day of a shorter month. |
| `--within <days>` | renewals | How far ahead to look (default 30). A charge today counts. |
| `--today YYYY-MM-DD` | list, renewals, export | Pretend today is another date. |
| `--file <path>` | all | Where your subscriptions are kept. Default: `$SUBTRACK_FILE`, else `./subscriptions.json`. |

## Money

Prices are typed in euros (`12.99`, `1,299.00`) and kept in whole cents. The monthly cost of a yearly plan is its
price divided by 12.

## Code

- `bin/subtrack.js`: the command line
- `src/cycles.js`: billing cycles: monthly cost and next charge of a plan
- `src/renewals.js`: upcoming charges
- `src/export.js`: CSV export
- `src/store.js`: reading and writing the subscriptions file
- `src/dates.js`, `src/money.js`: date and money helpers

Run the tests with `npm test`.

# subtrack

Keep track of your subscriptions from the terminal: what they cost you each month, and what renews next.
Plain Node.js (ES modules), no dependencies.

```sh
subtrack add Netflix 12.99                        # monthly by default, first charge today
subtrack add "Domain name" 14 --every year --since 2026-03-02
subtrack list                                     # every plan with its monthly cost
subtrack total                                    # what all of it costs you a month
subtrack renewals --within 14                     # charges coming up in the next 14 days, soonest first
subtrack export > subs.csv                        # CSV for a spreadsheet
subtrack remove Netflix
```

During development, run it with `node bin/subtrack.js <command>`.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--every week\|month\|year` | add | How often the plan charges you (default `month`). |
| `--since YYYY-MM-DD` | add | Date of the first charge (default today). Monthly and yearly charges fall on the same day of the month, or the last day of a shorter month; weekly charges fall every 7 days. |
| `--within <days>` | renewals | How far ahead to look (default 30). A charge today counts. |
| `--today YYYY-MM-DD` | list, renewals, export | Pretend today is another date. |
| `--file <path>` | all | Where your subscriptions are kept. Default: `$SUBTRACK_FILE`, else `./subscriptions.json`. |

## Money

Prices are typed in euros (`12.99`, `1,299.00`) and kept in whole cents. The monthly cost of a yearly plan is its
price divided by 12.

## Code

- `bin/subtrack.js`: the command line
- `src/cycles.js`: billing cycles: monthly cost and next charge of a plan
- `src/renewals.js`: upcoming charges
- `src/export.js`: CSV export
- `src/store.js`: reading and writing the subscriptions file
- `src/dates.js`, `src/money.js`: date and money helpers

Run the tests with `npm test`.

content.text:
`subtrack add "Meal kit" 59.90 --every week` now works, next to `--every month` and `--every year`. All 37 tests pass. I didn't run the CLI by hand, so the `add` → `renewals` flow is only covered by the new unit tests (weekly cost and 7-day charge dates).

- **Cost:** a weekly plan costs price × 52 ÷ 12 a month, so €12 a week is €52.00. Monthly costs now round to the nearest cent everywhere instead of being cut off. That also changes yearly plans: €119.99 a year now shows €10.00 a month, where it showed €9.99 before. I updated the one test that expected the old figure.
- **`total`:** it adds up the exact monthly amounts and rounds once at the end. This means the total can differ by a cent from the sum of the rounded figures that `list` shows.
- **`export`:** the CSV used its own copy of the monthly-cost calculation. It now uses the shared one, so it matches `list`.
- **Charge dates and `renewals`:** weekly plans charge every 7 days from `--since`, and `renewals` lists them like any other plan.
- **Other changes:** the usage text, the error for a bad `--every` value and the README are updated. I added tests for the weekly cost, the rounding and the 7-day charge dates.

I also fixed a bug in `renewals`. It sorted by the text label ("10 Nov" before "2 Nov"), which would have scrambled weekly plans. It now sorts by the actual date.
